Renderer for DirectDraw, Direct3D 1-7 and games run with WineD3D. Vulkan skips the OpenGL-on-Zink path and is much faster for old DirectDraw and Direct3D 7 games on Adreno.
Set to 1 to run Direct3D 8 through DXVK instead of WineD3D. Faster in AIO Graphics Test\'s Direct3D 8 test on Adreno.
Set to 1 to keep this game off ntsync (droiddeck-ntsync or a kernel driver); it uses droiddeck-esync where a pack exists, otherwise droiddeck-fsync.
Set to 1 to turn droiddeck-esync off for this game; it uses droiddeck-fsync instead, or droiddeck-ntsync where fsync is off too.
Set to 1 to keep this game off droiddeck-fsync; it uses droiddeck-esync where a pack exists, otherwise droiddeck-ntsync.
Set to 1 to run this game on droiddeck-fsync, or 0 to put droiddeck-esync first where a pack fits its Proton.
Set to 0 to disable Proton’s gamepad-navigation helper for this game.

On by default. Starts an Easy Anti-Cheat game without its anti-cheat when the game supports offline play. Turn off to launch through Easy Anti-Cheat as usual. Online modes that require Easy Anti-Cheat remain unavailable.

Renderer for Godot 4 games. auto runs Vulkan instead of D3D12, uses the Mobile renderer on PowerVR when the game uses Forward+, and saves Godot\'s pipeline cache more often. mobile or forward_plus picks the renderer, vulkan changes only the driver, and off leaves the game as it is. Launch options that pick a renderer always win.
DXVK overlay for D3D9–11. fps displays frame rate; unset hides it.
DXVK settings separated by semicolons. Recent builds use dxvk.maxFrameRate for frame limiting; prefer Steam\'s Quick Access menu frame limiter for ordinary play.
CPU cores for this game, such as 0-4 or 0,2,4, in place of the session\'s game cores. Fewer cores run cooler.

FEX keeps translated game code on storage so later launches skip translating it again. On by default for Slay the Spire 2; needs FEX-2609 or later in the game\'s Proton. Set to 0 if the game crashes after an update.

.NET tiering for games that ship coreclr.dll. pgo-off skips the instrumented tier; lean also compiles loops fully at once and tiers up sooner; single-tier compiles everything fully at first use, which starts slower but stutters less later. With the warmup experiment on, unset means pgo-off and off keeps the runtime\'s defaults.
D3D12 frame-rate limit. 0 disables the limit.

Cores this game\'s threads may run on. big keeps them off the little cores, a number keeps that many of the fastest, all uses every core. Windows sees only these cores, so engines start fewer worker threads.
Frame-rate cap for Godot, DXVK and VKD3D games, set at launch. A lower cap keeps the phone cooler and the frame rate steadier. Pick a divisor of the screen\'s refresh rate; 0 removes the cap.
Thermal governor for the frame cap: steps it down to 40 and then 30 fps while Android forecasts throttling, and back up once the phone cools. 0 keeps the cap fixed.
Ask for the slowest display refresh rate that fits the frame cap. 0 leaves the display rate to the session.
Set the performance hint target to one frame of the cap instead of 10 ms. 0 keeps 10 ms.
Mesa OpenGL threading. true can help CPU-limited OpenGL games; test per game.

Compress Steam while a game runs

Compresses Steam while a game runs, starting sooner when memory is tight. Steam is read back after the game closes once enough RAM is available. Turn this off if the session closes shortly after games start. A RAM cap above still compresses Steam when the session goes over it.

Applies while the Steam client runs. When the session uses more than this, Steam and then the session\'s other supported processes are compressed into zRAM. A soft cap: nothing is closed, but games may stutter while pages come back.
Needs zRAM swap, which this device does not have.

Reports this video memory budget to Direct3D 9 to 12 games to encourage lower memory use. Games may exceed it; this does not add GPU paging or guarantee protection from out-of-memory crashes. Takes effect at the next session.
Hold the GPU at its top clock
Adreno only. Fewer hitches, more battery use and heat.
Faster for the Steam client; in games the driver picks tile or system-memory rendering per pass. Required on Adreno 710/720/722.

A userspace stand-in for the Linux ntsync driver. While it is on, Proton uses it instead of droiddeck-esync and droiddeck-fsync. Works with Proton Experimental ARM64, GE-Proton and proton-cachyos. Applies next session.

Runs Proton\'s own fsync on the stock Proton files, with futex_waitv supplied in userspace, so it needs no pack and keeps working the moment Steam updates Proton. While it is on, games use it ahead of droiddeck-esync, except the few Proton keeps off fsync. Applies next session.

Games\' Windows threads wait on each other through eventfd and shared memory instead of round trips through wineserver. Uses a droiddeck-esync pack made for that exact Proton build; packs are fetched automatically. Until one exists for a new Proton build, droiddeck-fsync stands in. Applies next session.
Disables Proton\'s gamepad navigation helper, which costs CPU in every game.
May fix missing-syscall errors on some kernels. Can reduce performance.
